I have farmed this land for 50 years in Quzhou County. I am 73 now, finished middle school back in the commune days. My farm is only 4.1 mu, just me and my wife working it. I plant 2 mu of cotton for cash, 1.5 mu of mungbean — it fits in the rotation and the soil likes it — and 0.6 mu of millet for our own eating and some chicken feed.

For cotton, I always buy improved seed from the dealer in town. Last year I put down one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 16-16-16 kind — as base fertilizer, then top-dressed with urea twice, about 12 kg each time. That comes to roughly 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. This year I will do the exact same thing. My neighbor Old Wang tried to save 20 yuan per mu on fertilizer last year and his cotton dropped from 260 kg to 210 kg per mu. I am not taking that risk. Fertilizer is expensive now, around 120 yuan per mu for the chemicals, but a bad harvest is a disaster — I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose yield. I hire the rotary tiller from the village machine man, costs me 30 yuan per mu. I irrigate four times from the well: once at planting in late April, once at flowering in July, once at boll-setting in early August, and once more in late August if the weather stays dry. I spray pesticide five times, mainly for bollworm and aphids, starting about 10 days after first flower and then every two weeks. I expect 250 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather is normal.

For mungbean, I plant improved seed, about 3 kg per mu. Mungbean does not need much nitrogen — the roots make their own. I use 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, which is about 4 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium. I irrigate twice: at flowering and when the pods are filling. Two pesticide sprays for pod borer and aphids. I expect about 100 kg per mu. The mungbean stubble also helps the cotton plot next year.

For millet, I use my own traditional seed that I have saved for years — the local yellow millet that tastes good. I plant 0.6 mu. I put 25 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base and 10 kg urea when it is jointing — that is about 10 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations, one at jointing and one at heading. One pesticide spray for armyworm. Millet gives about 300 kg per mu on good land, so I will get around 180 kg total, enough for our household.

I think about every yuan. On 4.1 mu with only two of us, I cannot afford mistakes. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone in the village is spraying for bollworm, I spray too. Change is risky. I start from what worked last year and adjust only a little. That is how I have farmed for 50 years.
